follow-an-event.title: Filter and transform each event
follow-an-event.note: Read the predicate and mapper contracts: one decides which records continue; the other chooses the value emitted.
follow-an-event.question: Does filter change an accepted order into its output shape?
follow-an-event.answer: No. filter retains or drops the original item; map constructs the shaped value. Neither function makes a claim about broker delivery.

follow-an-event.title: Build and execute a bounded dataflow
follow-an-event.note: Follow the source, output and execution interfaces used by the editor and the course collect helper.
follow-an-event.question: Does constructing a Dataflow run the input immediately?
follow-an-event.answer: No. The graph is assembled first. The collect helper attaches a sink and calls run_main to execute it.

evolve-an-event-schema.title: A mapper applies your schema policy
evolve-an-event-schema.note: The callback implements normalization and rejection; Bytewax does not infer the amount units or schema version.
evolve-an-event-schema.question: If map receives version 2, does it know that amount is already in pence?
evolve-an-event-schema.answer: No. The normalize callback defines that interpretation. The operator applies the callback to each item.

evolve-an-event-schema.title: Finite test input
evolve-an-event-schema.note: Inspect how the fixed record sequence becomes the input to the graph.
evolve-an-event-schema.question: Does TestingSource validate each record against a business schema?
evolve-an-event-schema.answer: No. It provides the test items. The authored normalize function validates their fields.

read-a-partitioned-log.title: The Bytewax Kafka source
read-a-partitioned-log.note: Read how topics and partitions become input. The lab uses this connector against librdkafka’s simulator, not an Apache Kafka deployment.
read-a-partitioned-log.question: Does a record offset uniquely identify a record across all partitions?
read-a-partitioned-log.answer: No. It is a position within a particular topic partition; retain the partition as well.

read-a-partitioned-log.title: Send records and inspect offsets
read-a-partitioned-log.note: Inspect explicit partition selection and the delivery callback.
read-a-partitioned-log.question: Does returning from produce mean the record has been acknowledged by the broker?
read-a-partitioned-log.answer: No. produce queues a message locally. Polling or flushing serves delivery callbacks; inspect the delivery result.

stream-live-through-kafka.title: Consume and update live keyed state
stream-live-through-kafka.note: Follow how the child engine reads records, maintains keyed totals and reports observations.
stream-live-through-kafka.question: Which returned value retains the accumulator for the next record?
stream-live-through-kafka.answer: The first element of the stateful_map callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) pair.

stream-live-through-kafka.title: Produce a later event
stream-live-through-kafka.note: Read queueing, callback and flush behavior before treating a producer call as downstream completion.
stream-live-through-kafka.question: Does producer.flush prove the Bytewax result has reached the output?
stream-live-through-kafka.answer: No. It completes producer delivery work. This exercise separately waits for the engine’s observed result before sending another event.

retain-or-compact-a-log.title: Compaction is a log policy
retain-or-compact-a-log.note: Compare the broker’s documented compaction contract with the authored retained_log function. The Python helper does not run a broker compactor.
retain-or-compact-a-log.question: Is the retained value for a key necessarily the entire history for that key?
retain-or-compact-a-log.answer: No. A compacted view can retain the latest value while omitting earlier versions. Actual compaction is asynchronous; the helper’s deterministic result is a model.

give-consumers-their-own-position.title: Assign and commit a position
give-consumers-their-own-position.note: Read the distinction between fetching a record and recording the next offset for a group.
give-consumers-their-own-position.question: After processing offset 3, which offset should the group commit to resume after that record?
give-consumers-their-own-position.answer: Offset 4 in that topic partition. A committed position is the next offset to consume, not the last record’s offset.

route-and-quarantine.title: Separate good and invalid records
route-and-quarantine.note: The decoding callback labels the result; branch splits records according to a predicate.
route-and-quarantine.question: Does branch itself store invalid records durably?
route-and-quarantine.answer: No. It splits the stream. Durable quarantine requires an appropriate output and recovery policy.

expand-and-rekey.title: Change cardinality, then choose a key
expand-and-rekey.note: Read how flat_map emits several items per input and how key_on defines the accumulator’s ownership.
expand-and-rekey.question: Does doubling carts necessarily double the number of distinct product keys?
expand-and-rekey.answer: No. It can double line items while the same product keys receive more contributions. fold_final emits each final keyed accumulation when its finite input ends.

choose-the-right-clock.title: Engine clock contract for comparison
choose-the-right-clock.note: clock_windows is an authored assignment model. These engine clocks show how event timestamps and system time are selected in an actual window operator.
choose-the-right-clock.question: Does an EventClock always ignore wall-clock progress?
choose-the-right-clock.answer: No. Its documented watermark also depends on waiting duration and elapsed system time. The course’s frozen-clock fixtures control that progress explicitly.

close-a-window.title: Window membership and closing
close-a-window.note: Read window length, offset and the clock’s progress contract. The helper uses SlidingWindower even when slide equals width.
close-a-window.question: With length 10 and offset 5, can an event belong to more than one window?
close-a-window.answer: Yes. The overlapping windows can include the same event. Finite input completion can flush windows in this fixture.

merge-a-session.title: Sessions use a gap rule
merge-a-session.note: Read when events extend or merge a session and how the clock affects closure.
merge-a-session.question: Can a later-arriving event join two previously separate open sessions?
merge-a-session.answer: Yes, if its event timestamp bridges the configured gaps while both sessions remain eligible. A fixed tumbling boundary is a different membership rule.

wait-for-late-events.title: Watermark progress and late output
wait-for-late-events.note: Read the clock waiting duration and the window operator’s down and late outputs.
wait-for-late-events.question: Is wait_for_system_duration a guarantee that every older event will still be accepted?
wait-for-late-events.answer: No. Acceptance depends on the clock watermark and whether the relevant window has closed. The lesson exposes actual late output and controls system-clock progress.

correct-a-late-result.title: Framework late-data rules for comparison
correct-a-late-result.note: The corrections helper is an authored revision policy. Compare it with a framework’s window retention and late-data rules without treating them as the same API.
correct-a-late-result.question: Does changing allowed lateness automatically make every downstream sink interpret updates correctly?
correct-a-late-result.answer: No. The source policy and the sink’s revision/upsert contract must agree. Summing replacement totals as new contributions double counts.

keep-state-by-key.title: Key ownership and callback state
keep-state-by-key.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.
keep-state-by-key.question: Does returning None as updated_state retain the old state?
keep-state-by-key.answer: No. stateful_map documents None as discarding state. The emitted value is the second element, separate from retained state.

build-a-materialized-view.title: Store the latest accepted revision
build-a-materialized-view.note: The callback implements revision checks and tombstones; these are authored policies over native keyed state.
build-a-materialized-view.question: Does stateful_map automatically reject an older revision number?
build-a-materialized-view.answer: No. The application callback compares revisions and decides what to keep or emit.

enrich-a-stream.title: Look up a field in the mapper
enrich-a-stream.note: The mapper performs a Python dictionary lookup. This is a current local lookup, not a versioned temporal join.
enrich-a-stream.question: Does changing dict.get to direct indexing change Bytewax’s operator contract?
enrich-a-stream.answer: No. It changes the callback’s missing-key behavior: dict.get can supply a fallback, while direct indexing raises KeyError.

join-changing-streams.title: Join insertion and emission modes
join-changing-streams.note: Read insert_mode and emit_mode separately. This fixture chooses final emission over bounded input.
join-changing-streams.question: Does insert_mode="product" mean the operator automatically waits for an event-time horizon?
join-changing-streams.answer: No. It determines how values for a key are retained and combined. Emission mode and the input’s completion determine when this bounded fixture emits.

count-the-join-output.title: Interval join contract for comparison
count-the-join-output.note: interval_join is an explicit nested-loop course implementation. Use the framework guide to compare time bounds and retention requirements.
count-the-join-output.question: Can widening the horizon add output rows without adding comparisons in this helper?
count-the-join-output.answer: Yes. The helper still examines the same bounded candidate pairs; more of those pairs can satisfy the wider predicate.

look-up-the-past.title: Temporal joins and version history
look-up-the-past.note: temporal_lookup is an authored valid-time lookup. Compare its version selection with the documented temporal-table contract.
look-up-the-past.question: Can keeping only the newest region answer every late event correctly?
look-up-the-past.answer: No. A valid-time lookup needs the version effective at the event timestamp, plus a defined policy for missing history and historical corrections.

detect-event-sequences.title: Build an application state machine
detect-event-sequences.note: The callback tracks sequence history; this exercise does not invoke a built-in CEP engine.
detect-event-sequences.question: Does stateful_map infer which event sequence should trigger an alert?
detect-event-sequences.answer: No. The callback implements the sequence and time-horizon rules; filter selects the alerts it emits.

replay-without-double-counting.title: Deduplicate, then accumulate
replay-without-double-counting.note: Inspect identity selection, retained seen-state and final accumulation as separate operations.
replay-without-double-counting.question: If the identity key changes from event ID to shop, can valid orders be suppressed?
replay-without-double-counting.answer: Yes. The seen-state would then treat different orders from one shop as the same identity. The operator does not choose a business identity for you.

forget-state-deliberately.title: Key ownership and callback state
forget-state-deliberately.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.
forget-state-deliberately.question: Does returning None as updated_state retain the old state?
forget-state-deliberately.answer: No. stateful_map documents None as discarding state. The emitted value is the second element, separate from retained state.

forget-state-deliberately.title: State retention policy
forget-state-deliberately.note: The helper uses logical timestamps and returns None to discard state. It does not configure a background TTL service.
forget-state-deliberately.question: Does deleting seen-state preserve deduplication for arbitrarily late replays?
forget-state-deliberately.answer: No. Once an identity is forgotten, a later replay can appear new. Retention is part of the application’s correctness contract.

recover-after-a-failure.title: Configure real Bytewax recovery
recover-after-a-failure.note: Read recovery partition setup and the source snapshot contract. The helper waits for a checkpoint, kills the engine and restarts it within this one experiment.
recover-after-a-failure.question: Does recovering the source and keyed state make an append-only output file transactional?
recover-after-a-failure.answer: No. The file is outside the checkpoint commit boundary. Replayed input can repeat effects unless the sink has its own idempotency or transaction contract.

retry-with-a-budget.title: A mapper can implement retry policy
retry-with-a-budget.note: The retries are authored, bounded attempts with calculated delays. They are not built-in durable retries or measured sleeping time.
retry-with-a-budget.question: Does max_attempts automatically bound the entire service’s retry traffic?
retry-with-a-budget.answer: No. It bounds attempts in this helper. A service-wide budget must also account for concurrent work, retries at other layers and backoff scheduling.

measure-operation-effort.title: Python container operations
measure-operation-effort.note: The helper instruments explicit algorithms. A language reference describes operations; it does not promise universal constant-time performance for every key or implementation.
measure-operation-effort.question: Do the helper’s linear-scan comparison counts measure Bytewax’s internal lookup algorithm?
measure-operation-effort.answer: No. They measure the explicit course reference algorithm. Attribute complexity to the implementation actually counted, and separate retained identities from total events.

measure-latency-and-batching.title: Choose the measured boundary
links: Google SRE: latency, traffic, errors and saturation
measure-latency-and-batching.note: latency_run is a deterministic schedule model. Read the monitoring guidance before interpreting average completion, first-item delay or tail latency as interchangeable metrics.
measure-latency-and-batching.question: Does lower total elapsed time imply every item finished sooner?
measure-latency-and-batching.answer: No. Batching can improve overall completion while delaying the first item and increasing tail latency in this fixture.

when-the-consumer-falls-behind.title: Demand and bounded queues
when-the-consumer-falls-behind.note: queue_run is an authored admission/service model. It does not execute the Reactive Streams request protocol or measure a network queue.
when-the-consumer-falls-behind.question: Does increasing this model’s capacity fix a service rate below the offered rate?
when-the-consumer-falls-behind.answer: No. It can delay overflow for a finite burst while backlog keeps growing. Sustained overload requires admission, demand or service-capacity changes.

budget-for-recovery.title: Recovery capacity and state size
budget-for-recovery.note: recovery_capacity computes a fluid capacity model. Compare its spare-rate assumption with actual restore, replay and state-loading costs.
budget-for-recovery.question: Can the backlog shrink when service equals the offered rate?
budget-for-recovery.answer: No. There is no spare rate available to drain backlog. A recovery time also needs restore and replay behavior, not just a steady-state rate.

run-a-bounded-backfill.title: Read explicit partition offsets
run-a-bounded-backfill.note: Read the source range and distinguish consumed records from idempotent visible sink rows.
run-a-bounded-backfill.question: Does get_watermark_offsets return an event-time watermark?
run-a-bounded-backfill.answer: No. It returns low and high log offsets for a partition. The high offset is the next log position, not a timestamp completeness signal.

run-a-bounded-backfill.title: Transform the bounded input
run-a-bounded-backfill.note: The helper replays a bounded range and applies an authored sink keyed by record ID.
run-a-bounded-backfill.question: Does map itself prevent repeated writes from a replay?
run-a-bounded-backfill.answer: No. The sink policy determines whether repeated attempts create extra visible effects.

resolve-the-streaming-incident.title: Key ownership and callback state
resolve-the-streaming-incident.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.
resolve-the-streaming-incident.question: Does returning None as updated_state retain the old state?
resolve-the-streaming-incident.answer: No. stateful_map documents None as discarding state. The emitted value is the second element, separate from retained state.

resolve-the-streaming-incident.title: Separate operator state from application rules
resolve-the-streaming-incident.note: Identity checks, validation, late-event classification and output revisions are implemented in the callback.
resolve-the-streaming-incident.question: Does using a real stateful operator make every callback effect exactly once?
resolve-the-streaming-incident.answer: No. Checkpoint and sink-effect boundaries still matter. This bounded exercise demonstrates the authored policy, not a distributed transaction.
